hook: This dummy was blasted out of a jet on a rocket sled.
narration: This dummy was just blasted out of a jet cockpit racing down a rocket track.
This is the Holloman High Speed Test Track in New Mexico, a ten mile rail built for tests that are over in under six seconds.
Rockets shove sleds down these rails. The fastest runs here have passed nine thousand feet per second.
The riders are mannequins packed with instruments, because the Air Force no longer straps live people to this track.
At speed, the seat fires. [short pause] The dummy rockets up and out of the cockpit.
An ejection seat is its own small rocket. One pull of the handle throws the pilot clear of the jet, then opens a parachute.
Seconds later, the chute blooms over the desert.
outcome: The dummy drifted down under its chute, and the data went to the experts who check that these seats keep real pilots safe.
title: Ejection seat fired on a rocket sled
description:
At the Holloman High Speed Test Track in New Mexico, the Air Force's 846th Test Squadron fires ejection seats out of a cockpit mounted on a rocket sled, with instrumented mannequins in place of pilots.

Footage: U.S. Air Force video by Peter Ising, Airman Magazine, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/606101/holloman-high-speed-test-track-b-roll
